classification.difficultyReason: Use the statement that everyone studies at least one subject to infer the overlap, derive exclusive counts, and convert those regions to probabilities.

content.prompt: In a class of 26 students, 18 study chemistry and 12 study economics. Each student studies at least one of chemistry or economics.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Represent this information on a Venn diagram.

answer.short: Let $C$ represent chemistry and $E$ economics. Chemistry only: 14; both: 4; economics only: 8; neither: 0.
answer.worked:
Let $C$ represent chemistry and $E$ economics. Every student studies at least one subject, so $|C\cup E|=26$.

$$\begin{align*}|C\cup E|&=|C|+|E|-|C\cap E|\\26&=18+12-|C\cap E|\\|C\cap E|&=4\end{align*}$$

Chemistry only: $18-4=14$. Economics only: $12-4=8$. Neither: $0$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: One student is selected at random. What is the probability that the student studies:

answer.worked:
The overlap contains 4 students out of 26.

$$\begin{align*}P(C\cap E)&=\frac{4}{26}\\P(C\cap E)&=\frac{2}{13}\end{align*}$$

There are $12-4=8$ students who study only economics.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{only economics})&=\frac{8}{26}\\P(\text{only economics})&=\frac{4}{13}\end{align*}$$

There are $18-4=14$ students who study only chemistry.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{only chemistry})&=\frac{14}{26}\\P(\text{only chemistry})&=\frac{7}{13}\end{align*}$$
